LG-B-6017.$correct: It rises as the equilibrium interest rate rises
LG-B-6017.feedback: With a fixed quantity of money, higher demand raises its opportunity cost, the interest rate faced by borrowers.
LG-B-6017.commonError: Confuses demand for money with demand for interest-bearing bonds.

ECON-SP-MONETARY-POLICY-TRANSMISSION-603.q: In the scarce-reserves textbook model, monetary expansion lowers interest but firms do not increase investment. Which next part of the usual transmission chain is weakened?
options: The investment-driven rise in aggregate demand
The already-observed fall in interest
The definition of required reserves
The classification of currency in money
ECON-SP-MONETARY-POLICY-TRANSMISSION-603.$correct: The investment-driven rise in aggregate demand
ECON-SP-MONETARY-POLICY-TRANSMISSION-603.feedback: The chain from rates to investment fails to deliver the usual spending increase, so the investment contribution to AD is weaker.
ECON-SP-MONETARY-POLICY-TRANSMISSION-603.commonError: Assumes an observed rate cut guarantees a spending increase.

LG-B-6019.q: In a scarce-reserves textbook model, monetary expansion lowers rates and investment rises $10. With spending multiplier 2 and no other spending change, what AD effect follows?
options: A $20 decrease
A $20 increase
A $10 decrease
A $5 increase
LG-B-6019.feedback: The autonomous investment increase 10 is multiplied by 2, raising AD20.
LG-B-6019.commonError: Reverses the direction of expansionary monetary transmission.

LG-B-6020.q: In a scarce-reserves textbook model, monetary contraction raises rates and reduces investment $15. With spending multiplier 2 and no other spending change, what AD effect follows?
options: A $30 increase
A $30 decrease
A $15 increase
A $7.5 decrease
LG-B-6020.feedback: The autonomous investment reduction 15 produces a total demand reduction 30.
LG-B-6020.commonError: Reverses the direction of contractionary monetary transmission.

ECON-SP-FISCAL-POLICY-AD-SHIFT-6032.q: The government reduces purchases $20 during a recession. With spending multiplier 2 and no offsets, how does this affect the existing demand shortfall?
options: It widens the shortfall by $10
It has no effect because purchases are transfers
It widens the shortfall by $40
It narrows the shortfall by $40
ECON-SP-FISCAL-POLICY-AD-SHIFT-6032.feedback: The negative purchases impulse is multiplied:−20×2=−40. It reinforces a demand recession.
ECON-SP-FISCAL-POLICY-AD-SHIFT-6032.commonError: Treats a purchases cut as expansionary demand policy.

ECON-SP-TAX-CUT-AD-6033.q: A $100 tax cut raises disposable income. With MPC=.8, how much first-round consumption is added before induced spending rounds?
ECON-SP-TAX-CUT-AD-6033.feedback: First-round consumption=MPC×tax cut=.8×100=80. This is not yet the total multiplier effect.
ECON-SP-TAX-CUT-AD-6033.commonError: Treats the full tax cut as first-round consumption.

LG-B-6021.q: A tax cut produces an $80 first-round consumption increase. MPC=.75 with no other leakages or offsets. What total AD increase follows after induced rounds?
LG-B-6021.feedback: The spending multiplier is 1/(1−.75)=4; multiply the already-specified first-round impulse 80 by 4 to get 320.
LG-B-6021.commonError: Applies MPC again to an impulse already stated as consumption.

ECON-SP-CALCULATE-SPENDING-MULTIPLIER-60.q: With MPC=.8 and no offsets, what purchases increase is needed for a $100 total AD increase?
ECON-SP-CALCULATE-SPENDING-MULTIPLIER-60.commonError: Multiplies the target by the multiplier instead of dividing.

ECON-SP-CROWDING-OUT-EFFECT-6036.q: Fiscal expansion would add $100 to AD before crowding out. Higher rates reduce AD by a total $30 after induced investment effects. What net increase remains?
ECON-SP-CROWDING-OUT-EFFECT-6036.commonError: Adds crowding out to demand instead of subtracting it.

LG-B-6023.q: A demand gap is $250. Fiscal policy adds $300 gross to AD, while displaced investment reduces AD by a total $80 including induced effects. How much of the original gap remains in this fixed-price planning model?
options: $80 remains
$220 remains
$30 remains
$50 of excess demand appears
LG-B-6023.commonError: Uses the gross fiscal impulse instead of its net effect on the gap.
